strings.deepseek.budget.help: Filled in at the last 7 days’ daily average plus a fifth; change them as you like, or clear one to leave it off. Reminders only; requests are never blocked. Spend is what the account was charged (this Mac’s estimate plus spend not on this Mac); the week starts Monday 00:00.
strings.deepseek.choose_home: Choose the DeepSeek Harness data folder (usually ~/.dsh)
strings.deepseek.detected.account: Harness signs in with a DeepSeek account, so the balance is read after you sign in to the platform here.
strings.deepseek.detected.api: Harness uses an API key, so the balance is read with a key you paste here. Pacer does not read Harness’s own key.
strings.deepseek.detected.unknown: Harness has not used a DeepSeek model yet; web sign-in is used until it does.
strings.deepseek.dial_help: Today’s spend by hour on a 24-hour face, with the balance in the middle.
strings.deepseek.elsewhere_help: The account was charged this, but no task on this Mac accounts for it. Common causes: web search, background requests, or another device using the same account.
strings.deepseek.estimate_help: Spend is estimated on this Mac from token counts and published prices; the platform bill is authoritative.
strings.deepseek.key_help: The key is saved in your login keychain and used only to read the balance.

strings.deepseek.mode.balance_help: The dial shows today’s 24 hours of spend and the balance. Switch to Budget to set daily and weekly budgets: the dial then shows the budget left, DeepSeek can take a collapsed ring, and you are reminded at 80% and when over.
strings.deepseek.notice.budget_detail_day: %1$@ spent today of a %2$@ budget. Pacer only reminds; it never blocks requests.
strings.deepseek.notice.budget_detail_week: %1$@ spent this week of a %2$@ budget. Pacer only reminds; it never blocks requests.
strings.deepseek.notice.exhausted_detail: DeepSeek requests will fail until the balance is topped up.
strings.deepseek.notice.spike_detail: %1$@ in the last 10 minutes, over your %2$@ line.
strings.deepseek.panel_style_help: Detailed adds where the money went and the last 7 days, which appear once two earlier days had spend.
strings.deepseek.peak_hours_help: Peak price (×2): Beijing weekdays 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00, shown in your time zone. Weekends and 2026 public holidays are off-peak.
strings.deepseek.pricing_note: Costs are estimated on this Mac from token counts and DeepSeek’s published prices: doubled on Beijing weekdays 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00, off-peak on weekends and 2026 public holidays (make-up working days count as weekends, so this is an estimate). Web search costs ¥5 per 1,000 calls from 1 Nov 2026. Only DeepSeek’s own channels are estimated; your platform bill is authoritative.
strings.deepseek.ring_hint.inner: The collapsed inner ring shows the budget left.
strings.deepseek.ring_hint.none: No collapsed ring shows the budget yet.
strings.deepseek.ring_hint.outer: The collapsed outer ring shows the budget left.
strings.deepseek.runway_help_days: At %1$@ a day, the balance lasts about %2$ld days.
strings.deepseek.source.web: DeepSeek platform, signed in on the web
strings.deepseek.speed_basis_help: This Mac estimates from tasks here and updates with every reply. Account counts balance changes, including other devices and web searches, about once a minute, and needs a connected balance. Speed bars and the spend-spike alert follow this.
strings.deepseek.speed_help: Spend in each 10 minutes of the last 2 hours (%@), newest on the right. The dashed red line is the spend-spike line (%@ in 10 minutes).

strings.whats_new.app_buttons: Open Codex or Claude from the island
strings.whats_new.app_buttons_detail: Buttons beside Mark All as Read in the expanded island bring each service’s desktop app forward, even with no task running. Turn them off here or in Settings > General.
strings.whats_new.child_endings_detail: Ended Codex subagents no longer appear to run again after Pacer reconnects, wakes or relaunches.
strings.whats_new.claude_next_step_detail: When Claude Desktop ends a turn by asking you to choose the next step, the task shows as finished and Pacer reminds you to reply.
strings.whats_new.cloud_coordination_detail: Pacer reminds you when a thread needs a decision or a reply and when it is resolved, and a resolved thread you read in Claude clears here. A thread shows an estimated speed while it writes a reply, and the real speed when its turn ends.
strings.whats_new.cloud_projects_detail: Threads and coordinators from your Projects now appear in the task list, with a cloud icon and the project’s name. They use your claude.ai sign-in; turn them off in Settings → Claude.
strings.whats_new.day_dial: A day dial for the DeepSeek balance
strings.whats_new.day_dial_detail: Today's spend by hour, the doubled-price hours and the balance in one ring. Sign in on the web or paste an API key, matching how Harness signs in.
strings.whats_new.deepseek_alerts_detail: A flame appears when 10 minutes cost more than your line. Balance changes are reconciled with this Mac’s estimate, so web search or another device shows up as spend not on this Mac. One alert shows at a time, and notifications can open Harness or the top-up page.
strings.whats_new.deepseek_budget_detail: Set daily and weekly budgets. The expanded panel can show them as a split ring like Codex’s 5h and week, and DeepSeek can take one of the collapsed rings; choose which module goes outside and inside.
strings.whats_new.deepseek_clock_detail: With DeepSeek alone, the collapsed bar shows a price clock: peak hours outside, spend inside, the hand at now. Pricing knows 2026 public holidays and estimates only DeepSeek’s own channels.
strings.whats_new.deepseek_detail: DeepSeek Harness joins Codex and Claude: stages, speed, approvals, questions and endings, with each turn's estimated cost.
strings.whats_new.dual_orbit: A smoother badge with both services
strings.whats_new.dual_orbit_detail: When Codex and Claude run together, both arcs around the task badge keep a clean head and their own places, and grow or fade smoothly as tasks start and end.
strings.whats_new.free_move_detail: Drag the status bar to place the island where you want it. Release near a screen edge to snap. Free Move replaces the fixed positions in Appearance.
strings.whats_new.mark_all_read_detail: Clear every ended task at once, on all pages, with the new button next to the pin. Tasks that are running or waiting for your reply or approval stay in the list.
strings.whats_new.open_at_login: Start Pacer with your Mac. You can change this anytime in Settings > General.
strings.whats_new.remote_control_detail: Recognize devices by name and see whether they are online, offline or waiting for a session.
strings.whats_new.screen_position_detail: Choose Custom in Settings > Appearance to keep it below the menu bar or dock it as a slim strip in any corner of the screen, handy on Macs without a notch.
strings.whats_new.split_quota: Both quota windows in one ring
strings.whats_new.split_quota_detail: The expanded island puts 5-hour quota in a shorter upper arc and 7-day quota in a longer lower arc, each with its own percentage, reset countdown and pace tick. With one service on, its pace, reset time and forecast sit beside the ring. Switch to Classic anytime in Settings > Appearance.
strings.whats_new.stability_detail: More reliable remote task monitoring, with completed cards staying read after you open their conversations.
strings.whats_new.subagent_endings_detail: A Claude Code subagent that finishes while its chat is busy no longer stays running, and the speed keeps updating while only subagents work.
strings.whats_new.task_models: Model and reasoning effort on every task
strings.whats_new.task_models_detail: Each task row shows its model and reasoning effort below the speed.
strings.whats_new.task_rows_detail: Turn time sits beside the speed, status icons are outlines, and endings you have seen fade back.
strings.whats_new.third_party_claude: Claude and Codex tasks from third-party apps
